name: Sarah H. Wu
title: PhD student in Media Psychology
bio: I research the psychology of technology use. I care about identifying and addressing situations where technology has the potential to undermine human capacities. Some questions I explore include: What are the long-term consequences of using chatbots to navigate social situations or our work? In an algorithmically curated media environment, how can we provide better content recommendations beyond bans and screen time limits?

Before starting my PhD, I earned my BA in Psychology from Reed College in Portland, OR. I also worked as a predoctoral research fellow at the Stanford Institute for Research in the Social Sciences (IRiSS), assisting with research in the Social Media Lab.

Outside of research, I play violin semi-professionally in Argentine tango ensembles across the Bay Area. I also volunteer for the Peninsula Symphony through their school outreach program, which brings live music to students in underserved communities.
